title: Rollout Orchestration Workbook (cross-team labs) - WIP
body:
Purpose:
Quick-working workbook for coordinating cross-functional rollouts and A/B/canary experiments. This is intentionally lightweight — capture decisions, guardrails, telemetry, and contact points. Use for feature launches that touch runtime, model, and routing.

Status / context:
- Draft, iterating with Eng SRE and ML teams (notes from 2025-01 design shop).
- This doc is the canonical short-form operational checklist for the first 72h of exposure for small->medium canaries.

Primary goals (what success looks like):
- No customer-facing latency/SLA regressions outside agreed tolerance during ramp.
- Detect and contain model-quality regressions quickly (automated prompts + human triage).
- Clear owner and rapid rollback path for each release slice.
- Experiment analysis plan defined up front (metrics, sample size, stopping rules).

Scope (what this workbook covers):
- Cross-team coordination: product, serving-runtime, SRE, ML, QA, data privacy, support.
- Canary selection, cohort sizing, ramp schedule, telemetry thresholds, escalation ladder.
- A/B analysis basics and quick post-launch checks.

Out of scope (for this document):
- Long-running multivariate experiments (>4 weeks) — use the Experiment Platform playbook.
- Legal/compliance approvals (assume approvals already acquired for private deployments).

Quick glossary (team shorthand we use here):
- rollout lead: primary PM or PM+engineer who owns the exposure plan.
- rollback buddy: engineer assigned to execute fallback if needed.
- deck: the short one-pager for exec ops.

Stakeholders / roles (template to fill for each rollout):
- rollout lead: (name)
- ML owner: (name)
- on-call SRE: (name, pager)
- infra/serving runtime owner: (name)
- product support liaison: (name)
- legal/privacy contact: (name)
- data/metrics analyst: (name)

Decision log (example entries) — fill at kickoff:
- 2025-01-15: Use traffic thermostat routing, initial cohort 0.5% global traffic, 24h observation window. -- Maya
- 2025-01-18: Increase to 2% after no signals. Add eval set A for relevance drift. -- Ethan

Cohort selection heuristics (how to pick canary slices):
- Start with low-business-impact segments (read-only, free tier, mobile web) unless core flows are affected.
- Prefer cohorts that are geographically consistent to avoid cross-region noise.
- If feature touches authentication or billing, start in internal-only cohort via feature flag.
- Exclude high-risk customers (compliance-sensitive) via routing policy.

Ramp schedule patterns (pick one):
- Tiny-sprint: 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% (24h windows, 48h before 50%).
- Confidence ramp: 0.5% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% (48h windows).
- Timeboxed aggressive: 1% -> 10% -> 50% (only for urgent ops with full on-call coverage).
Notes: pick windows based on traffic volume and sample size needs (see A/B analysis).

Telemetry & guardrail signals (primary + secondary):
Primary (auto-trigger rollback):
- SLO latency (p95) increase > 15% absolute relative to baseline over observation window -> immediate throttle to previous model variant.
- Error rate delta (5xx or inference faults) > 0.5 percentage points absolute -> stop ramp and investigate.
- Production mem/cuda OOMs or queue growth > 3x baseline -> fallback to older serving config.

Secondary (requires human review):
- Quality regression detected on evaluation prompts: automated eval mean relevance drop > 3 points or top-k accuracy delta > 2% -> alarm to ML owner.
- User-reported regressions (support tickets trending) -> escalation to product + ML.

Telemetry sources (where to look):
- Console dashboards: per-route latency, token-cost breakdown, error traces.
- Canary-specific slices in tracing (use tag release=<id>).
- Auto eval harness results (nightly + during ramp) posted to S3 and slack.
- Support tag stream (#support-rollouts).
- Billing usage (to detect cost spikes).

Traffic control primitives (what we can change quickly):
- Feature flag toggle (on/off) — fastest, use for internal-only cohorts.
- Traffic thermostat: route X% to new model variant with gradual increase.
- Region pinning: move canary to a single region for isolation.
- Model variant fallback: route to quantized/cheaper or older checkpoint variant when latency increases.

Experiment measurement plan (A/B basics to pre-register):
- Primary metric: synthetic quality score on preregistered prompt set (describe set id), or customer-specific conversion metric if available.
- Secondary metrics: p95 latency, token cost per request, error rate, CSAT/NRR if tracked.
- Minimum detectable effect: define MDE before launch (recommend at least 1-2% uplift for product metrics or 3-5% relative for automated quality metrics).
- Sample-size calc: do a quick calc with baseline rate and MDE — if traffic insufficient, extend window or increase cohort.
- Statistical approach: prefer Bayesian posterior/simulation for sequential stopping. Predefine stopping rules (e.g., posterior probability > 0.95 that variant is better) and safety checks.

Stopping & rollback procedure (short):
1) Rollout lead declares stop.
2) Rollback buddy flips feature flag OR routes 100% to last stable model.
3) On-call SRE pins config and creates incident channel.
4) ML owner runs quick evals on latest set and posts findings.
5) If rollback was triggered by latency/error: collect traces, heap/cuda logs, and file a follow-up.
6) Postmortem required if customer impact > threshold (see postmortem template).

Escalation ladder (who to call, in order):
- 0-30m: rollout lead + rollback buddy (Slack + pager).
- 30-120m: on-call SRE + infra lead + ML owner.
- >120m: Eng director + Product director + Legal (if PII or regulated customers impacted).

Quick-run checklist (to tick before starting ramp):
- [ ] Pre-registered experiment and metric definitions saved (link).
- [ ] Feature flag ready and tested in staging.
- [ ] Observability dashboards created and annotated.
- [ ] Rollback test verified (toggle on/off in staging).
- [ ] Pager assigned and contact list confirmed.
- [ ] Data retention and privacy check completed for this rollout.

Unresolved questions / discussion items (workshop):
- How to automatically tie the auto-eval harness to the decision matrix for small quality deltas? (Priya to prototype).
- Should we enforce a mandatory 24h quiet window after rollouts that touch billing?
- Experiment analysis: prefer exposing result digest in Console — who owns the UI?

Postmortem template (short):
- Summary (what happened, impact).
- Timeline (key events, who did what).
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence.
- Immediate mitigations.
- Long-term fixes (owner + ETA).
- Lessons & changes to the workbook.

Example mini-case (sketch):
- Feature: new reranking model (quantized checkpoint v2).
- Cohort: 0.5% mobile traffic in eu-west1.
- Ramp: 0.5% -> 2% -> 5% (24h windows).
- Primary metric: relevance score on seed set (id: rerank-A).
- Guardrails: if p95 latency +20% OR relevance drop > 4 -> immediate rollback.
- Outcome: week 1, no latency signal, but automated eval showed 3.8 drop; escalate to ML for quick tuning; held at 2% until fix.

How to use this doc in practice:
- Make a copy per rollout and fill template fields above. Keep the copy linked from the rollout registry.
- Live-edit the "Decision log" during the first 72 hours so postmortem is easier.
- Use Slack incident channel naming convention: #rollout-<feature>-<YYYYMMDD>.

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Build small automation to push the experiment pre-registration to Console and create dashboards automatically.
- Add a lightweight web form for rollout lead to declare readiness; triggers SRE checklist.
- Consider a guardrail that automatically reduces traffic when cost/token spikes > 2x baseline for > 15m.

References and useful links:
- Experiment registry (Confluence) -> TODO link above.
- Trace tag conventions: release_id, experiment_id, cohort.
- SRE runbook for infra health checks (linked in registry).

Last edited: 2025-02-03 by Maya Singh

---
End of workbook (copy this file for each new rollout; keep original as template).
